title: Senior Backend Engineer — Payments Infrastructure, AI Driven
description:
## About the Role

We're building a global payments platform — API-first, modeled after Stripe — and hiring our first engineer. The founder built the entire product with AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor). The platform is live: full merchant API, dashboards, payment orchestration, documentation, CI/CD. Now we need a senior engineer to own production reliability, code quality, and infrastructure decisions as real merchants onboard and real money moves.

This is not a "write CRUD endpoints" role. AI generates the majority of the code. Your job is to review it, catch the edge cases that cause double-charges or race conditions, ensure zero-downtime migrations, and be the person who knows exactly what to do when payments break at 2 AM.

You'll inherit a mature codebase and a disciplined engineering process — not a blank slate — and extend both as the team grows.

---

## What You'll Do

- **Review and harden AI-generated backend code daily** — mandatory type-check gates, no empty catch blocks, no parseFloat on monetary values (everything is integer cents)
- **Own production monitoring, alerting, and incident response** — Sentry, structured logging (zerolog), on-call
- **Manage database performance** — query optimization, migration safety, connection pooling on Neon serverless (dual-driver: HTTP reads, WebSocket transactions)
- **Operate and upgrade Hyperswitch** — our open-source payment orchestrator running on Docker/Railway; you'll manage the service lifecycle and eventually own its Kubernetes migration
- **Make infrastructure decisions** — scaling strategy, service boundaries, deployment pipeline improvements
- **Ensure payment flow correctness** — idempotency, state machine transitions, settlement reconciliation, ledger integrity
- **Own secrets and environment management** — Doppler sync across Railway, Vercel, and AWS
- **Keep engineering documentation current** — architecture decisions, runbooks, API contracts live in Outline and must stay in sync with the code

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| API Server | **TypeScript**, **Hono.js** v4.6+, Zod validation, `@hono/zod-openapi` |
| ORM / Database | **Drizzle ORM**, **PostgreSQL 16** (Neon serverless — dual-driver: HTTP reads, WebSocket transactions) |
| API Gateway | **Go 1.22+**, Upstash Redis rate limiting, zerolog structured logging |
| Payment Orchestration | **Hyperswitch** (Rust, Docker) with Stripe connector |
| Workflow Engine | **Temporal Cloud** — webhook delivery, payment sagas, retry logic |
| Frontends | Next.js 15, Tailwind v4, Clerk auth, shadcn/ui |
| Infrastructure | **SST Ion**, Vercel, Railway, **AWS ECS Fargate**, GitHub Actions CI/CD |
| Edge / Async | **Cloudflare Workers**, Cloudflare R2, Cloudflare Queues |
| Secrets | **Doppler** (synced to Vercel, Railway, AWS Secrets Manager) |
| Monitoring | Sentry (Node.js + Go) |
| Cache | Redis (Upstash) |
| Monorepo | pnpm workspaces, git worktrees |

---

## Required

- **5+ years backend engineering**
- **TypeScript** — advanced: you can read Hono.js routes, Drizzle schemas, and Zod validators without ramp-up time
- **PostgreSQL** — deep: query tuning, transaction isolation levels, zero-downtime migrations, connection pooling
- **Production operations** — you've been on-call, triaged multi-service incidents, built monitoring and alerting from scratch
- **Docker** — comfortable managing and debugging containerized services
- **CI/CD** — GitHub Actions or equivalent; you understand what happens when a deploy breaks
- **Monorepo experience** — pnpm workspaces or equivalent; you know how to work cleanly across package boundaries
- **Comfortable reviewing AI-generated code** — not just "using Copilot," but auditing code that AI wrote from spec to production: catching type gaps, missing error paths, incorrect assumptions about external APIs

## Strong Bonus

- **Go** — our API gateway is Go; you don't need to be expert but readable is the bar
- **Payments / fintech domain** — PSP integrations, idempotency patterns, ledger design, reconciliation
- **Temporal** or any workflow engine — Temporal Cloud is core to our async flows
- **Kubernetes** — Hyperswitch migration to ECS/K8s is on the roadmap
- **Cloudflare Workers** — we're expanding edge usage
- **Hyperswitch** or any open-source payment orchestrator experience

## Not Required

- Degree or certifications
- FAANG pedigree
- Having used this exact stack before — a strong engineer ramps fast

---

## What Makes This Role Different

**You're engineer #1, not engineer #50.** There's no existing engineering culture to inherit — you build it. That means your judgment on code quality, incident response, and system design becomes the default.

**The AI workflow is real, not a talking point.** Claude Code runs with mandatory checkpoints: type-check gates before every commit, PROGRESS.md files tracking every agent's work, multi-agent sessions across git worktrees. You'll be the human in that loop — reviewing diffs that span six files written in parallel by subagents, catching the edge cases the model didn't see.

**The work is consequential.** Payments are unforgiving. A bug in an idempotency key means a merchant gets charged twice. A botched migration means downtime. You'll write the runbooks, own the alerts, and be accountable when things break — because you're also the one who prevented most of it.

**No process overhead.** No sprint ceremonies, no tickets, no design-by-committee. You see a problem, you fix it. That's liberating and demanding in equal measure.

**Equity that means something.** First engineering hire at an early-stage payments company. Generous allocation, standard vesting, priced at the ground floor.

---

## What We're Not

We won't pretend this is easy. You're joining a two-person team (founder + you) with real merchants and real money on the platform. There's no senior engineer above you to escalate to. If you need extensive mentorship, a large team to distribute risk across, or a mature engineering org to learn from, this isn't the right fit yet.

If you want maximum ownership, minimum bureaucracy, and to build something that ships — this is it.

## Plus
Equity is available
A lot of incentives to grown
Project is backed with funds and founder expertise

title: Glide Developer for Warehouse Order Verification App
description:
We are looking for an experienced Glide developer to build a simple internal mobile-friendly warehouse order verification app.

The app will be used by warehouse checkers to verify that items on an order were picked correctly. Glide is a fit because it supports barcode scanning, user accounts, linked data, computed columns, and workflow/actions.

What the app needs to do

The workflow should be very simple:
1.	User signs in
2.	User scans or enters an Order Number
3.	App loads and displays all expected items on that order
4.	User scans a product barcode
5.	App looks up that barcode in a Barcode Lookup table
6.	App returns the matched internal Item Number
7.	App checks whether that item belongs on the active order
8.	User enters a Qty to Add
9.	App saves that as a transaction
10.	Order line progress updates to show ordered / scanned / remaining / status

This is not a customer-facing order tracking app. It is an internal warehouse checking app.

Important requirements

The app must support:
•	Glide native sign-in for approved users only
•	Mobile-first layout
•	Barcode scanning
•	Multiple possible barcodes mapping to the same item
•	Quantity entry after scan, instead of forcing the user to scan each unit
•	Clear validation messages such as:
o	Unknown barcode
o	Item not on this order
o	Quantity exceeds remaining
•	Running totals by order line

Glide supports private/user-based app access and ties users to email-based accounts, but it does not natively use traditional username/password authentication.

Data structure required

Please build around these 5 tables:
1. Orders
•	OrderID
•	CustomerName (optional)
•	OrderDate (optional)
•	Status (optional)
2. OrderLines
•	OrderLineID
•	OrderID
•	ItemNumber
•	ItemName
•	QtyOrdered
Computed:
•	QtyScanned
•	RemainingQty
•	LineStatus
3. BarcodeLookup
•	Barcode
•	ItemNumber
•	BarcodeType (optional)
•	Notes (optional)
One item may have multiple valid barcodes.
4. ScanTransactions
•	TransactionID
•	OrderID
•	ScannedBarcode
•	MatchedItemNumber
•	QtyAdded
•	CheckerEmail
•	Timestamp
•	IsValid
•	Message
5. UserState
•	Email
•	CurrentOrderID
•	LastScannedBarcode
•	QtyToAdd

Computed/helper columns as needed.

Logic requirements
•	User scans a barcode
•	App resolves barcode through BarcodeLookup
•	App returns internal ItemNumber
•	App verifies that item is on the current order
•	If valid, user can enter qty and save
•	Each save creates a new row in ScanTransactions
•	QtyScanned on OrderLines should be calculated from transaction totals, not manually stored as a running value

Screens

We only need 2 main screens:

1. Start Order Check
•	Scan or enter order number
•	Validate order exists
•	Load order
2. Check Order
•	Show all order items
•	Show ordered / scanned / remaining / status
•	Scan barcode
•	Show resolved item
•	Enter qty to add
•	Save transaction
Nice if you have experience with
•	Glide relations
•	Glide query columns
•	Glide computed fields
•	Glide actions/workflows
•	Warehouse/inventory/picking apps
•	Barcode-based operational apps
Deliverables
Please provide:
•	Completed Glide app
•	Final table schema
•	All computed columns used
•	All actions/workflows used
•	Setup instructions for importing orders, order lines, and barcode lookup data
•	Notes on any assumptions made

To apply

•	Estimated cost

If you have experience building warehouse, picking, scanning, inventory, or verification apps in Glide, please mention that specifically.

title: Software Architect - Productionize AI Automation Platform
description:
About Us

We're building an AI-operated company. A 3-person CPG brand sold through major US retailers, where AI agents handle the work that would normally require a team of 15+: content creation, social media, customer outreach, product discovery, financial modeling, and autonomous pipeline monitoring.

Over the past 6+ months, our CEO built 9+ AI automation systems using AI coding tools (Claude Code). We already have an autonomous AI agent that runs 24/7, delivering morning briefs, monitoring all pipelines, and alerting via Slack on a 2-hour heartbeat. The vision is to deploy autonomous agents across every function of the business.

The systems work and deliver real operational leverage. But they were built through rapid experimentation and need production-grade architecture to support the next wave: more agents, more autonomy, more reliability.

This engagement was scoped by a Fortune 50 AI & technology executive who will oversee the build and review all deliverables. We're looking for top candidates who can defend their architectural decisions to senior technical leadership.

What Exists Today

- 9+ production automation systems (100+ Python scripts) running on a Mac Mini M4
- 20+ daily cron jobs across content, social, monitoring, and reporting
- Integrations with: Google Sheets, Slack, Meta Graph API, TikTok, multiple retail APIs
- Engineering practices: deployment scripts, post-deploy verification, health monitoring, AI-assisted code review
- An autonomous AI agent (24/7) delivering briefs, monitoring pipelines, alerting via Slack
- Multiple systems making LLM calls (Claude, GPT) for content generation, scoring, and decision-making
- Knowledge base: 100+ documented lessons from production incidents

What's Missing

- No version control (no git)
- No CI/CD (manual SCP-based deployment)
- Flat directory structure (no packages or modules)
- Systems operate in silos (don't coordinate with each other)
- Google Sheets as primary data store
- Only the CEO can operate, debug, or deploy (bus factor of 1)
- API keys hardcoded in scripts
- Scripts fail silently with no alerting
- No standardized patterns for AI agent deployment or LLM integration
- No framework for scaling from 1 autonomous agent to many

What We Need You to Build

Phase 1 - Automation Audit & Mapping
- Inventory all automations, map dependencies between systems
- Define core data objects and integration points
- Produce a technical blueprint the non-technical team can read

Phase 2 - System Architecture Design
- AI agent infrastructure: patterns for deploying, monitoring, and coordinating autonomous agents across business functions
- LLM integration layer: standardized patterns for AI calls, prompt management, cost tracking, output validation, and retry logic
- Design workflow orchestration supporting both fully autonomous and human-in-the-loop operations
- Design shared modules (Sheets, Slack, scraping, etc.) so new tools reuse existing work
- Integration layer so systems coordinate instead of operating in silos
- Deployment and rollback that a non-engineer can execute
- Data layer strategy (reduce Google Sheets dependency, define where operational state lives)
- Guardrails: auth, cost limits, approval gates

Phase 3 - Workflow Refactoring
- Modularize scripts into packages
- Add retry/failure handling
- Create reusable components
- Enforce shared schemas across systems

Phase 4 - Observability & Cost Controls
- Structured logging
- One-place visibility into what ran, what succeeded, what failed
- Dead-pipeline detection and alerting
- Cost tracking for API usage

Critical Constraints (read carefully)

1. The team is non-technical. The CEO builds with AI coding tools. The cofounder and ops specialist are not engineers. Everything you build must be operable by non-engineers with AI assistance. If your architecture requires an engineer to maintain it, you've failed.

2. AI-assisted development continues. The CEO uses AI coding tools (Claude Code) as his primary development tool. This will continue after your engagement. Your architecture must create patterns that make AI-assisted development faster and more reliable, not harder. Think: clear module boundaries, consistent naming, documented interfaces.

3. The codebase is Python. It stays Python. Don't propose a rewrite in another language.

4. Infrastructure migration is expected. The current production environment is a Mac Mini M4 on a home network, primarily hosting an autonomous AI agent. We want to reduce dependence on this setup. Your architecture should include a migration path to sustainable, cloud-friendly infrastructure.

5. The platform must stand on its own. An outside engineering team should be able to evaluate, understand, and operate it without the founder. Your deliverable should include a technical narrative documenting the full architecture.

6. Don't over-engineer. We are 3 people, not 300. If you're thinking Kubernetes, microservices, or infrastructure-as-code, this isn't the right engagement. We need organized, documented, observable Python with clean deployment. That's it.

Ideal Candidate

- 7+ years Python in production
- Has architected systems for small teams or startups (not just enterprise)
- Can design for a team scaling from 3 to 5 (we plan to hire an engineer after this engagement)
- Has built systems that non-engineers operate day-to-day
- Experience designing systems where AI agents operate autonomously (not just AI-assisted tools)
- Understanding of LLM integration patterns: prompt management, cost controls, output validation
- Comfortable with AI-assisted development (the CEO builds with Claude Code daily)
- Strong written communication. You'll produce documentation a business operator reads, not just code
- Bonus: experience with automation/workflow orchestration (cron-based, event-driven)

How We'll Work

- Phase 1 is a paid trial. You'll audit the codebase, produce a blueprint, and we'll evaluate fit.
- If Phase 1 goes well, we proceed to Phases 2-4 on an hourly basis.
- Communication via Slack. Daily check-ins with the CEO (hands-on founder).
- Full codebase access from day one.
- We'll share our existing productionization plan as your starting framework.
- Final deliverable includes a technical narrative documenting the full architecture, suitable for review by outside engineering leadership.

To Apply

Skip the generic cover letter. Instead, answer these three questions:

1. What would you specifically NOT build for a 3-person non-technical team running Python automations on a Mac Mini?
2. Describe a time you architected a system that a non-engineer operates day-to-day. What made it work?
3. What's your honest reaction to a codebase of 100+ Python scripts in a flat directory with no git? What's your first move?

title: Automation Specialist for Course Operations (WordPress, HighLevel, LearnWorlds, Google Docs, Make)
description:
Job Description

We are a professional continuing education institute that provides advanced clinical training courses for dentists. We are seeking an experienced automation specialist to build a streamlined system that automates student registration workflows, email communication, webinar access, and document generation across our platforms.

Our goal is to reduce manual administrative work and create a reliable automated experience for every course cohort.

The automation should connect WordPress, HighLevel, LearnWorlds, Google Docs/Drive, and payment triggers to manage the full student lifecycle—from registration to course completion.

---

Current Tech Stack

* WordPress (course pages and registration)
* Stripe / Affirm (payments)
* HighLevel (CRM, email automation, pipelines)
* LearnWorlds (on-demand webinars and learning portal)
* Google Docs / Google Drive (documents and templates)

The system will likely use Make.com (Integromat) or a similar integration platform as the automation engine.

---

Scope of Work

1. Student Registration Automation

When a student registers on our WordPress website:

* Automatically create or update the contact in HighLevel
* Tag the contact by course and cohort
* Record course date and registration details
* Trigger the onboarding email sequence

---

2. Automated Email Sequences (HighLevel)

Create automated emails for:

Immediately after registration

* Registration confirmation
* Course logistics and next steps

Course reminders

* 14 days before course
* 7 days before course
* 3 days before course
* 1 day before course

These emails should include course information, logistics, and preparation instructions.

---

3. LearnWorlds Webinar Access Automation

Students receive access to on-demand webinar content related to their course.

Access rules:

* Access begins 2 weeks before the course
* Access ends 2 weeks after the course

Automation should:

* Enroll the student in the correct LearnWorlds course
* Send the access email
* Automatically remove access after the allowed period

---

4. Google Docs / Google Drive Document Automation

Create automated document generation using Google Docs templates.

Documents to generate automatically:

* Student name tags
* Course certificates / diplomas
* Student rosters
* Attendance sheets

Documents should:

* Pull student data automatically
* Generate PDFs
* Save files in the correct course folder in Google Drive

---

5. Post-Course Automation

After the course:

* Send thank-you email
* Send certificate/diploma
* Move contact into alumni segment in HighLevel

---

Deliverables

* Fully automated workflow connecting WordPress, HighLevel, LearnWorlds, and Google Docs
* Email automation sequences configured in HighLevel
* Webinar access automation configured in LearnWorlds
* Document generation system using Google Docs templates
* Clear documentation of the workflow so our team can manage it

---

Requirements

* Proven experience with automation platforms such as Make, Zapier, or similar
* Experience integrating WordPress with CRM systems
* Strong experience with HighLevel automation
* Experience with LearnWorlds or LMS integrations
* Experience generating documents using Google Docs automation
* Ability to design clean, reliable automation workflows

---

Nice to Have

* Experience working with education platforms or course providers
* Experience with Stripe-triggered automation
* Experience building student lifecycle automation systems

---

Project Type

Initial project: Automation system setup

Potential for ongoing work and additional automation projects as our programs expand.

---

Timeline

Preferred completion timeline: 2–4 weeks

---

Required Screening Questions

Please answer the following questions in your proposal.

1. Automation Architecture

If a student registers for a course on a WordPress website, how would you automate the workflow so that:

* the contact is created in HighLevel
* the student receives confirmation emails
* LearnWorlds access begins 2 weeks before the course
* access is automatically removed 2 weeks after the course

Briefly describe the automation flow you would build.

---

2. Document Automation

Have you created automated document generation using Google Docs or Google Slides templates?

If yes, explain how you generated documents such as certificates, PDFs, or name tags automatically.

---

3. Automation Platforms

Which tools have you used to build automation systems between platforms such as:

* WordPress
* CRM systems
* learning platforms
* document systems

Examples may include Make, Zapier, APIs, or webhooks.

---

4. Relevant Projects

Please provide 2 examples of automation systems you built that involved multiple platforms (website + CRM + email + documents).

---

Important

Please start your proposal with the word “Automation” so we know you read the full job description.

Proposals that do not include answers to the questions above will not be considered.

This project is bigger than just connecting Twilio. We need someone who understands WooCommerce workflows, database/data structure, automation triggers, webhooks, and SMS event handling.

Our goal is to build a backend system that can:

track customer lifecycle stages

trigger automated SMS messages based on WooCommerce events and timing

update customer data/status automatically

pause or change workflows when customers reply

create a cleaner automation-ready backend for future scaling

WooCommerce supports workflow-based automations through AutomateWoo, including triggers, rules, actions, and Twilio SMS integration, and Twilio supports webhooks/status callbacks for two-way messaging and delivery tracking. We want someone who can either build around those tools or recommend a stronger custom architecture if needed.

Scope of Work
1. WooCommerce Backend Cleanup

Review and improve backend structure for:

customer records

order data

phone number formatting/validation

tags, statuses, or custom fields

workflow-ready data organization

We want the store/backend set up so automations can reliably know things like:

new client

first order date

last order date

active member vs non-member

reorder window

needs follow-up

replied / needs manual review

2. Workflow / Automation Engine

Set up an automation layer that can trigger actions based on:

new order

completed order

account creation

membership signup

time elapsed after purchase

no reorder after X days

reply received by SMS

This can be built with:

AutomateWoo workflows

WooCommerce hooks/webhooks

custom backend logic

or a hybrid approach

AutomateWoo officially supports workflow automation using triggers, rules, and actions, and also supports Twilio SMS integration, so experience with that is preferred.

3. Twilio SMS Integration

Set up or repair Twilio so the site can:

send automated SMS

log outbound messages

receive inbound replies

track delivery status

trigger actions from replies or status changes

Twilio webhooks are required for this because Twilio sends real-time callback events to your application for incoming messages and status updates.

4. Required Automation Flows

Initial flows we want live:

New client welcome SMS

3-day follow-up

7-day follow-up

reorder reminder

membership / support reminder

pause automations when customer replies

5. Database / Data Update Logic

We need backend automation so customer records are updated automatically when actions happen.

Examples:

mark customer as “new client” after first order

stamp first order date

stamp last SMS sent date

mark “replied” if SMS response comes in

pause future automated sends if reply received

mark reorder due after defined time window

This can be done with custom fields, post meta, user meta, or a more structured database layer — developer should recommend the best path.

6. Admin Visibility

Need a simple way for our team to see:

what automation a customer is in

what texts were sent

whether they replied

whether automations are paused

what follow-up is next

7. Compliance / Messaging Controls

System must support:

opt-in tracking

STOP / START / HELP handling

unsubscribe logic

message suppression after opt-out

Deliverables

WooCommerce backend reviewed and cleaned up for automation readiness

Twilio connected and functioning

automation/workflow system configured

customer data/status updates automated

at least 4–6 active SMS workflows

reply handling and pause logic working

documentation/SOP for our team

recommendations for scaling future automations

Preferred Skills

WooCommerce

WordPress backend development

AutomateWoo

Twilio API

webhooks / status callbacks

automation architecture

database / custom field structure

customer lifecycle automation

Screening Questions

What We Want Built First

Phase 1 should include:

backend data cleanup

Twilio repair/setup

workflow engine setup

4 core SMS automations

reply pause logic

basic admin visibility

Internal Note for Developer

We are looking for someone who can help us create a long-term automation structure, not just install a plugin. The right person should understand the relationship between:

WooCommerce customer/order data → workflow triggers → Twilio SMS events → backend status updates

That’s the real project.

We need someone who can think through the full automation architecture, not just basic Twilio connection. Our main need is backend workflow automation tied to WooCommerce customer/order data, with Twilio used as the outbound/inbound messaging layer.

• Progress walkthroughs (verify work is being completed)

• Re-inspections (if work was not completed correctly)

• Assign the walkthrough
• Store notes, photos, and videos
• Track feedback
• Track which inspection stage the job is in

• Skills / trade type
• Jobs completed
• Reliability
• Deadlines met vs missed
• Communication quality
• Responsiveness
• Photo/video submission reliability
• Payments made to them

The system should help identify patterns over time so I can see who performs best and predict who is best for future jobs.

• Contractors invited to bid

• Follow-ups required to receive bids
• Bid pricing
• Which bid was accepted
• Which bids were negotiated
• How often a contractor’s bid gets selected

	5.	Bid approval
	6.	Active work
	7.	Inspection
	8.	Re-inspection (if needed)
	9.	Completion

At any time I want to see:

• Current stage of every job

• Deadlines

For each job:

• Tasks must be assigned

• All parties should clearly see what they are responsible for

• Client payments

• Overdue payments

Payments should also link to:

• Specific job

• Client

7. Client Profiles

Each client should have a profile that tracks:

• Jobs they submitted
• Jobs that moved forward

• Communication patterns
• Pricing

8. Employee & Team Tracking

I want to track internal team performance.

Track:

• Tasks assigned

• Tasks overdue
• Time taken to complete work
• Follow-ups required
• Mistakes and wins

This helps identify strengths, weaknesses, and performance trends.

⸻

9. Notifications & Alerts

The system should automatically alert when:

• Tasks are overdue
• Milestones are approaching
• Payments are late
• Approvals are missing

⸻

10. Document Management

The system should store all project documents including:

• Contracts
• Scope of work documents
• Invoices
• Permits
• Photos
• Videos

⸻

11. Reporting & Dashboards

I want dashboards that show:

• Active jobs
• Job stages
• Financial summaries
• Contractor performance
• Employee performance
• Client activity trends

⸻

12. Workflow Automation

If possible, I would like automation such as:

• Automatically moving jobs through stages
• Creating follow-up tasks
• Sending notifications when milestones are due
• Assigning tasks automatically

⸻

13. SOP Integration

I want to attach Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to tasks and stages so projects are completed consistently.

⸻

Track:

• Inventory

• Returns
• Leftover materials

This helps ensure we always know what materials we have available.

Technology

title: Full-Stack SaaS Developer — Swiss ESG Compliance Platform for SMEs (MVP to Full Product)
description:
Full-Stack SaaS Developer — Swiss ESG Compliance Platform for SMEs (MVP to Full Product)

Project Overview:
I am building a Swiss-hosted ESG compliance SaaS platform for Swiss SMEs (5–50 employees) and fiduciaries (Treuhänder) who manage multiple client mandates. The platform helps Swiss SMEs document ESG reporting, LkSG/VSoTr supply chain compliance, and sustainability requirements from banks and large customers.
This is a multi-tenant B2B SaaS application. Think of it as a compliance management tool where one fiduciary manages 10–30 SME clients from a single dashboard.
Inspiration/Reference products: ZEROvia (zerovia.ch), Plan A, Normative — but focused exclusively on the Swiss fiduciary channel and LkSG compliance, which none of these cover adequately.

Tech Stack (required):

Frontend: React or Vue.js
Backend: Node.js (Express) or Laravel (PHP)
Database: PostgreSQL
Hosting: Infomaniak (Switzerland) — mandatory for Swiss data protection law (nDSG)
Authentication: Auth0 or Supabase Auth
PDF Generation: Puppeteer or PDFKit or WeasyPrint
Email/Notifications: Postmark or Mailgun
File Storage: Infomaniak Swiss Object Storage (S3-compatible)
AI Integration: Anthropic Claude API (claude-sonnet) for document extraction
XBRL Export: EFRAG Digital Template format (same standard as ZEROvia)
Payments: Stripe (CHF currency)
Background Jobs: Bull (Node) or Laravel Queues for automated reminders and annual reports


Features Required:
Module 1 — ESG Core (MVP — build first)

Guided VSME Basic + Comprehensive data entry form (step by step, one question at a time)
Help text on every field explaining where to find the data
CSV upload for bulk data entry
Automatic PDF report generation (VSME format, OR 964j format)
XBRL export (EFRAG Digital Template — same as CSRD-standard)
Gap indicator — traffic light system showing missing mandatory fields
ESG Score 0–100 with breakdown by E, S, G dimensions
Year-on-year progress comparison

Module 2 — Supply Chain

Curated database of 50+ large Swiss companies (Migros, SBB, Coop, Nestlé etc.) and their specific ESG requirements
Side-by-side requirement comparison tool
«Does my ESG report cover what this customer needs?» checker

Module 3 — Retention & Task Management

Task management system with assignable deadlines
Automatic email reminders before deadlines
Automatic annual report generation trigger (January each year)
Progress dashboard per mandate

Module 4 — LkSG/VSoTr Compliance (MVP — build first)

Guided due diligence questionnaire (German Supply Chain Act)
Documentation PDF generator — audit-ready output
VSoTr (Swiss supply chain ordinance) compliance check
Complaint mechanism documentation template
Risk country flagging for supplier countries

Module 5 — Banking Export

Formatted ESG report export specifically for Swiss banks
ZKB format compatibility
Raiffeisen format compatibility
«Bank-ready» one-click export

Module 6 — Visibility & Benchmarking

Public sustainability profile page at yourplatform.ch/company-name
Shareable link replacing PDF email attachments
Anonymous peer benchmarking by industry (NACE code — same methodology as ZEROvia, active after 100+ customers)
Internal fiduciary leaderboard showing ESG scores across all mandates
AI-assisted data entry: user uploads existing documents (annual report, invoices), Claude API extracts relevant ESG values, human confirms before saving

Module 7 — EU Ecodesign Product Pass

Digital product pass generator (EU Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781)
Auto-generation from existing ESG data already in the system — zero double entry
QR code output linking to machine-readable product data
PDF version for attaching to delivery documents
Fields: CO₂ per unit, materials with origin, repairability index, recycled content percentage

Module 8 — Materiality Analysis

Double materiality questionnaire (25–30 guided questions, CSRD/ESRS standard)
Two dimensions scored: impact materiality (outside-in) + financial materiality (inside-out)
Automatic materiality matrix visualization
PDF export — audit-ready documentation
Integration with Module 1: after analysis, gap indicator only flags truly material fields as mandatory


Multi-Tenant Architecture (critical requirement):
This is the most important technical requirement. The system has two user roles:
Fiduciary role: Sees all their client mandates in one dashboard. Can switch between clients. Can compare clients. Manages deadlines across all mandates. White-label option (their own logo on client-facing reports).
SME role: Sees only their own company data. Fills in their ESG report. Downloads their documents.
Reference architecture: similar to how accounting software like Bexio handles multi-client fiduciary access.

General Technical Requirements:

Multi-tenant with full data isolation between tenants
Swiss data hosting mandatory (Infomaniak) — nDSG (Swiss GDPR equivalent) compliant
ISO 27001 compatible data handling
Mobile responsive (fiduciaries often work on tablets)
Secure login with 2FA option
Audit logs for all data changes
White-label PDF reports for fiduciary branding
GDPR + nDSG compliant data deletion and export


Regulatory Standards the platform must support:

VSME Basic and Comprehensive (EFRAG standard for SMEs)
Swiss OR 964j (Swiss Code of Obligations sustainability reporting)
LkSG (German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act)
VSoTr (Swiss Supply Chain Ordinance)
EU Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781
CSRD Double Materiality (ESRS standard — for Module 8)
GHG Protocol (Scope 1, 2, 3 emissions calculation)


What I need from you:

Fixed price offer broken into milestones (Module 1+4 MVP first, then phases)
Realistic timeline estimate per phase
2–3 examples of previous SaaS platforms you have built with login, multi-tenant, PDF export
Your recommended tech stack with reasoning
Your experience with Swiss hosting (Infomaniak) or willingness to deploy there
Your availability per week in hours

Budget:
Open to phased approach. Please provide two numbers: full project estimate and MVP-only estimate (Module 1 + Module 4). I am building phase by phase as revenue comes in.
I am open to a phased development approach — starting with Module 1 and Module 4 as MVP, then expanding phase by phase as revenue comes in.

and we expect you to figure out the best path to get there. If you 
need step-by-step instructions to do your job, this is not the right 
role for you.

---

WHO YOU ARE

You are not a developer who learned automation on the side.
You are an automation operator who thinks in systems, speaks fluent

can be eliminated.

  require it

  your own solutions before presenting them

Most importantly: you understand that the goal is not to build 
automations. The goal is to book meetings for our clients at scale, 
with excellence. Every decision you make flows from that objective.

You have done this kind of work before - for clients, for employers, 
for your own projects. You have proof. You have results. And now you 
want to stop juggling multiple gigs and go all-in on one role where 
you can make a real strategic difference.

WHAT MAKES THIS OPPORTUNITY DIFFERENT

Most automation roles pay you a flat rate to execute tasks someone 
else defined. This is not that.

At devlo, your compensation grows directly with the value you create:

- Base: $2,000/month (this is the starting point, not the ceiling)
- Variable: performance-based bonuses tied to objectives in the 
  first phase
- Long-term: as you prove your impact, you access a revenue share 
  on new clients signed

To put that in perspective: our average client contract is 
$40,000-$50,000 CHF/year. A 10% bonus on a single new client is 
$5,000. The right person will not be earning $2,000/month for long.

We are generous with people who deliver. We are looking for someone 
who wants to earn like a partner because they perform like one.

---

SELECTION PROCESS

We receive a high volume of applications. Many are automated. 
We do not have time for that, and neither do you.

Here is how we filter:

STEP 1 - Loom video (mandatory)
Record a 2-minute Loom video. Show us one real problem you solved 
for a client or employer. What was the situation, what did you build, 
what was the result. We want to see how you think, how you communicate,

No video = no review. No exceptions.

STEP 2 - Technical assessment
If your video impresses us, we will give you a real problem from our

STEP 3 - Conversation with Charles (founder)
If the test confirms what the video promised, we talk. We align on 
expectations, compensation structure, and whether this is the right 
fit on both sides.

---

TO APPLY

Send your application with:
1. Your 2-minute Loom video (mandatory)
2. A brief description of your current tool stack
3. One specific result you are most proud of

We read every application that includes a video. We respond fast

devlo is based in Switzerland. Our clients are international.
